input.quote: 21.2 Each Patty agrees to indemnify each of the other Parties in respect of all costs, expenses, damages and demands, arising out of or in connection with any claim against, or liability of, the latter as an owner of APCN 2 where such claim is made by, or the liability is to, any third party not being a Party hereto and arises out of or in connection with APCN 2 provided that no indemnifying Party shall be obligated to contribute more than its share of liability as per Schedule B.
input.rationale: This is a consortium construction and maintenance agreement for APCN 2, not a vendor/customer supply contract: there is no counterparty acting as Vendor, and the equipment vendors contract separately with the Procurement Group under the Supply Contract. Teleglobe USA and the other APCN 2 Parties are co-owners with several (not joint) liability, so the indemnity architecture is necessarily mutual. Paragraph 21.2 gives us an indemnity from every other Party for all costs, expenses, damages and demands arising from any third-party claim connected with APCN 2 — wording broad enough to capture third-party intellectual property infringement claims against us as an owner — and Paragraphs 32.1 to 32.4 supply the standard procedure (notice to the Management Committee, no admission or settlement without approval, and compliance with conduct directions), with sharing in Schedule B proportions. Each Party's exposure is capped at its Schedule B Investment Share, which is the consortium analogue of the fallback's super-cap and is proportionate to what we receive. The clause therefore meets the fallback on its material terms: we obtain third-party claim (including IP) indemnity coverage from the counterparties, subject to a proportionate cap and standard claim-handling mechanics. Two sub-elements fall short of the preferred position and are noted rather than flagged: IP infringement is not expressly enumerated, and there are no procure/modify/replace/refund remedies. Because the obligation runs to our benefit as much as against us and reflects the agreed consortium bargain, no redline is warranted.
